g.text: Cloudflare admin token (account-owned, made by hand)
Terraform manages DNS, buckets, the watchdog and the panel's login in Cloudflare with this token.
mcctl's admin token is account-owned, so it can never act on another account. mcctl can't create
it for you: Cloudflare doesn't let a token made through the API manage tokens, and this one must
(it creates the bucket-only R2 credentials). Dashboard path: Manage Account > Account API Tokens
Open the pre-filled form and pick the account that owns tests.mcctl.internal:
Check the permissions: exactly the 8 rows in the table below, nothing else (each row:
Account/Zone, the permission, Read/Edit; the form may say Write for Edit).
Account Resources (if shown): Include > the account that owns tests.mcctl.internal. Zone
Resources: Include > Specific zone > tests.mcctl.internal (not All zones).
Client IP Address Filtering: leave empty (CI runners change addresses). TTL: start today, end
about a year ahead (mcctl doctor warns 30 days before it expires).
Continue to summary > Create Token, then paste the token below (input hidden; saved to .env
look-alike: the two Zone rows need the FIRST dropdown set to Zone (the Account list has no DNS,
look-alike: Zone > DNS, not Zone DNS Settings, Account DNS Settings, DNS View or DNS Firewall
look-alike: Zone > Zone, not Zone Settings
look-alike: the combined Access: Apps and Policies, not Access: Apps or Access: Policies
look-alike: the combined Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups, not Access:
mcctl checks the token live and compares its permissions with the table (missing, extra, wider).
Cloudflare token: account-owned, active, expires 2027-10-01; zone tests.mcctl.internal found;
R2, Workers, D1 and token permission groups reachable
account-owned token: exactly the permissions mcctl needs, on tests.mcctl.internal and its
Domain auto-renew: if tests.mcctl.internal is registered with Cloudflare, switch auto-renew on
in the dashboard (Domain Registration > Manage domains > your domain > Auto-renew); mcctl
doesn't hold a registrar permission. `mcctl doctor` and the weekly expiry check watch the expiry
The admin panel's login (one-time PINs to your email) runs on Cloudflare Zero Trust.
global session 24h -> 15m (it bounds how long after your last one-time PIN Access may open the
confirmation host without a new one; your panel login keeps its own 24h session)
Terraform's state (the only secret store) lives in a private R2 bucket with a bucket-only token.
created an API token that can only read/write objects in e2e-tfstate
the state credentials can use bucket e2e-tfstate

Check the permissions against the table below, then Generate token.

edvardk/smallworld shares its workflows with your repositories (user)
mcctl-e2e/e2e-mc-config: rulesets available (main gets the pull-request + checks ruleset)
mcctl-e2e/e2e-mc-config: forking off (a fork would carry the config repo's history)
mcctl-e2e/e2e-mc-config: auto-merge allowed, merged branches deleted (the update PRs, P11)
GitHub App for the admin panel's whitelist pull requests: one click in your browser creates it
with exactly these permissions; then you install it on the config repo only.
Your browser opens a page from mcctl: click 'Create the GitHub App on GitHub'.
On GitHub: check the name, then Create GitHub App (private, no webhooks).
Next, GitHub's install page: Only select repositories > mcctl-e2e/e2e-mc-config, nothing
panel App: GitHub App e2e-panel: exactly contents write, metadata read, pull_requests write
e2e-panel is installed on mcctl-e2e/e2e-mc-config only (checked as the App)
GitHub App for the weekly update pull requests (lock files, product version): one click in your
browser creates it with exactly these permissions; then you install it on the config repo only.
Your browser opens a page from mcctl: click 'Create the GitHub App on GitHub'.
On GitHub: check the name, then Create GitHub App (private, no webhooks).
Next, GitHub's install page: Only select repositories > mcctl-e2e/e2e-mc-config, nothing
updater App: GitHub App e2e-updater: exactly contents write, metadata read, pull_requests write,
e2e-updater is installed on mcctl-e2e/e2e-mc-config only (checked as the App)
